05/ 10.07.2025 Heard the parties.

2. This anticipatory bail application under Sections 482 and 484 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita (Bnss), 2023, has been preferred by the petitioner apprehending his arrest for offences
registered under Sections 420/466/467/468/469/ 471/34 of the Indian Penal Code pending in the
court of learned S.D.J.M., Rajmahal in connection with Complaint Case No. 816 of 2017 arising out
of Rajmahal Ps Case No. 39 of 2016 corresponding to G.R Case No. 91 of 2016.
3. Learned A.P.P. representing the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail.
4.  Admittedly complaint petition was filed which was referred under section 156(3) of Cr.PC for registering the FIR.
After the FIR was registered the police investigated the occurrence and filed the Final Report exonerating the petitioner.
5. The informant thereafter filed a complaint protesting the filing of the Final Report.
Abadh Lal Mehta vs The State Of Jharkhand.

6. On the basis of the said complaint, the court examined the enquiry witnesses, thereafter the court has taken cognizance of the offence and issued summons to the petitioner.
The petitioner thereafter has approached this Court by filing anticipatory bail.
7. Since the petitioner was exonerated in the investigation and cognizance has been taken thereafter on the 2025:JHHC:18585 complaint/protest there is no scope of any investigation further.
8. Thus, the petitioner should answer the summons and appear before the court concerned.

Once the petitioner appears before the court concerned, the concerned court will pass appropriate order in terms of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of "Satender Kumar Antil vs. CBI and Anr." reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51 .
